title: Work around the absence of SpeculationReasonEncoding in OpenJDK11

timeline.body:
Fixes #2933

Note that this PR fixes only the specific issue discussed in #2933, which is necessary to create a Mandrel build based on graalvm's master.  Even after merging this PR parts of GraalVM will fail to build using OpenJDK 11, for instance `mx --primary-suite-path substratevm --components='Native Image' build` will fail.
This and `getEntryPoint` are `final` in vanilla openjdk11
This is still an early version to get some feedback. Error checking will be improved once we agree on the core changes.
Proxy and reflection accessors will eventually be cached in static variables as requested in https://github.com/oracle/graal/issues/2933#issuecomment-714362574

reply.body: Please do cache the proxy class `Proxy.newProxyInstance(...).getClass()` in a `static final` field. Reflection accessors do not need to be cached as long as its arguments are compile-time constants.

timeline.body: I am not sure about this. Please make sure to review thoroughly.
SVM code should not be referenced in non-SVM projects.

What I had in mind was to access `UnencodedSpeculationReason` fields `context` and `groupId` reflectively from the code in `com.oracle.svm.graal.isolated`, and to call the `SpeculationReasonEncodingClone` methods directly. This has the advantage that the native image build can reliably turn the reflective accesses into direct field accesses.
Alternatively, you could move `SpeculationReasonEncodingClone` to `org.graalvm.compiler.serviceprovider` as `UnencodedSpeculationReasonEncoding` and use it just the same as `SpeculationReasonEncoding` in `DirectSpeculationReason`. That just leaves introducing a proxy needed to support both types of `SpeculationReason` depending on the JVMCI version.
Should we cache the encodings here?

reply.body: Looks like we can only do that using a `WeakIdentityHashMap`, but I wouldn't now unless it proves to have a performance impact.
Not sure how to benchmark this. I will be happy to if you provide instructions though :)

Hi @peter-hofer could you please let me know if this is moving in the right direction?
Remove `throws` clause: does not throw these exceptions any longer.
Should be a cast to `Character`.
Must use `getDeclaredField`: these fields are package-private.

Must use signature for lookup and pass receiver:
```
                IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding encoding = (IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding) Class.forName("jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason").getDeclaredMethod("encode", Supplier.class)
                                .invoke(reason, new SpeculationReasonEncodingSupplier(speculationReasonEncodingProxy));
```
Probably best to just do `PROXY_CLASS.getDeclaredConstructor(...).newInstance()` here so the native image build can fold the reflective instantiation.

reply.body: I cached the constructor as well.

timeline.body: The `invoke` call is missing a receiver of type `IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding`, which should first be instantiated in the supplier and passed to this invocation handler class via a constructor.

reply.body:
I doubt the image build can optimize the reflective accesses, and on top of repeatedly doing lookups at runtime, we will need to register the methods of `IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding` as reflectively accessible in a `Feature` during the image build.
So I'd rather avoid this proxy, but I don't see how we can have a class that directly implements `SpeculationReasonEncoding` when that interface cannot be referenced in the code.

@peter-hofer is there any way to inject this interface to `SpeculationLog` when using an openJDK which lacks it (using something like `com.oracle.svm.core.annotate.TargetClass#onlyWith`)

Alternatively, could we add the interface in the sources and compile it in only when needed? (possibly through mx).

> The invoke call is missing a receiver of type IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding, which should first be instantiated in the supplier and passed to this invocation handler class via a constructor.

Shouldn't the said `IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding` be instantiated for each new encoding and as a result don't we need a new `SpeculationReasonInvocationHandler` for each new encoding and consequently a new proxy instance rendering https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/2945/files#r519816278 impossible?

> Shouldn't the said `IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding` be instantiated for each new encoding and as a result don't we need a new `SpeculationReasonInvocationHandler` for each new encoding and consequently a new proxy instance rendering https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/2945/files#r519816278 impossible?

I agree, we do need a separate instance of each of these classes for each encoding operation. Not sure what that contradicts, I think you meant to link to a comment.

> @peter-hofer is there any way to inject this interface to `SpeculationLog` when using an openJDK which lacks it (using something like `com.oracle.svm.core.annotate.TargetClass#onlyWith`)
> 
> Alternatively, could we add the interface in the sources and compile it in only when needed? (possibly through mx).

Using substitutions is a clever idea, but they don't support changes to the class hierarchy. What we could try is substituting methods of the dynamic proxy class to call the encoder directly instead. Substituting a generated class like a proxy sounds a bit fragile, though.

> > Shouldn't the said `IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding` be instantiated for each new encoding and as a result don't we need a new `SpeculationReasonInvocationHandler` for each new encoding and consequently a new proxy instance rendering https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/2945/files#r519816278 impossible?
> 
> I agree, we do need a separate instance of each of these classes for each encoding operation. Not sure what that contradicts, I think you meant to link to a comment.

It looks like after force pushing changes links to out-of-date discussions break :man_facepalming: 
New link after force pushing is https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/2945#discussion_r519816278

I could use `java.lang.reflect.Proxy#getProxyClass` to get the proxy class and cache it but it is deprecated.

Edit: NVM I think I figured how to do this without using `getProxyClass`

> I doubt the image build can optimize the reflective accesses, and on top of repeatedly doing lookups at runtime, we will need to register the methods of `IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding` as reflectively accessible in a `Feature` during the image build.
So I'd rather avoid this proxy, but I don't see how we can have a class that directly implements SpeculationReasonEncoding when that interface cannot be referenced in the code.

@peter-hofer please have a look at https://github.com/zakkak/mandrel/commit/19398016bc4bf77061268db7f5395ebd9286ebb6, it removes the proxy and relies solely on our cloned interface.
If the original `encode` gets invoked elsewhere it will essentially generate the same encoding and cache it in the corresponding `EncodedSpeculationReason` instance.
If I am not mistaken this should work without the performance penalty.

FYI: The full diff of this approach against master can be seen [here](https://github.com/oracle/graal/compare/master...zakkak:no-speculationreasonencoding-for-openjdk11-v2)

> @peter-hofer please have a look at [zakkak@1939801](https://github.com/zakkak/mandrel/commit/19398016bc4bf77061268db7f5395ebd9286ebb6), it removes the proxy and relies solely on our cloned interface.

Looks good. I did encounter problems when the proxy class is created at image build time, so that's another reason to avoid it.
However, I would like to have two separate code paths which directly call `UnencodedSpeculationReason.class.getDeclaredField("...").get*(reason)` and `Class.forName("jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason").getDeclaredField("...").get*(reason)` and pass the values to a method that does the encoding. That way, we can be sure that these reflective accesses will become direct field accesses during the image build.
My only worry other than that is that `EncodedSpeculationReason` may be changed in the future and this code silently becomes broken, which would have been prevented by using a proxy class.

> My only worry other than that is that `EncodedSpeculationReason` may be changed in the future and this code silently becomes broken, which would have been prevented by using a proxy class.

Yes I also thought about this, but even with the proxy in place this would still be the case for the `UnencodedSpeculationReason` path, right?
I guess we should implement some kind of test and add it to `mx gate` so that if/when `EncodedSpeculationReason` changes we get notified (the simplest I can think of is comparing the result of the copied methods with the result of the corresponding methods in `EncodedSpeculationReason`).
@peter-hofer the test is now added to the PR, I hope this is enough to detect potential future changes in `EncodedSpeculationReason` that could cause issues.

timeline.body: Please name this method `encodeAsByteArray`.

There is a (significant) chance that this class is initialized during the image build and not only when encountering a class other than `UnencodedSpeculationReason` at runtime, in which case this will likely break the image build. Therefore, we have to just set all the static fields to `null` in that case.
Converting to draft till I get the test working.

If I understand the review conversation, these reflective accesses will be converted to non-reflective accesses during image building. A comment should be added somewhere here explaining that. Does the added unit test check that this happens?
I'll run our tests on the current state and let you know.

Looks good overall, but there is another problem: for JDK 8, we have a class `GraalServices.EncodedSpeculationReason` which the current code tries to cast to `jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason` and fails.
@dougxc , how come we need that extra class on JDK 8 rather than using `jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason` or `UnencodedSpeculationReason` like on JDK 11?
I cannot recall the reasons. I think using `jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason` should work.

timeline.body:
Thank you @olpaw and @dougxc

I made `GraalServices.createSpeculationReason()` use  `jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason` and removed `GraalServices.EncodedSpeculationReason`.
I changed the compliance level of the junit tests I added to "8+" so that we can use them for both JDK 8 and 11.
I also augmented the native junit test to test `GraalServices.createSpeculationReason()` as well.
